I'm 6'4", and this is my story on how I got in shape.

18 months ago, I weighed in at 270 lbs. I ate shit. I was single, felt insecure in the bedroom (although I have a decent sized cock) and decided to make a change.

Mind you, I am a lazy computer programmer. I didn't want a fad diet or the like. I didn't want to change my eating. There just had to be a way to hack this. And I did.

I researched for weeks and started reading about intermittent fasting. One particular flavor, the Fast 5 is one I decided to try. The idea is this: Normally at night while you're sleeping, you don't eat. And ideally that would be a 12-hour window that you don't eat. (And you break your fast with breakfast, get it?) So, you increase that 12-hour window to 19-hours. That's it. There is a 5-hour window in which you can eat whatever you want, as much as you want. I chose my window to be 5-10pm, as that is when I was going out with friends, etc. Oh, and outside your eating window, you can consume zero-calorie liquids: black coffee, diet soda, water, tea.

I eased in to it by taking lunch later and later over the course of 2 weeks. At first, when 5pm rolled around, I'd gorge on something like: a whole pizza, 2 cheeseburgers, a burrito or two, a tub of ice-cream and the like. And at 10pm, I stopped eating.

The weight fell off before my eyes. I was losing about 5 pounds a week. After a while, I hit a plateau at around 220lbs. Also, I should note that during this time, my stomach started shrinking. I once tried eating two double cheeseburgers back to back and puked. It was too much food. So, I also started eating healthier. My "go-to" dinner consisted of a spinach salad, simple dressing, steak and an avocado. I slowly cut out dairy and white flour from my diet.

I stopped the intermittent fasting once I plateau'd for a while, and stayed at that weight, more or less. Once you get to a plateau, your body will tend to "snap" back to that weight, even if you indulge now and again.

Then, I decided I wanted to lose the gut and started hitting the gym. Every. Damn. Day. It sucked. I had a belly, felt fat and out of shape. But I stuck with it.

I've been doing this now for 1 month, and today I weighed in at 202 lbs and 13% body fat. Still a little on my tummy, but by the end of the summer, I'll have a six-pack and will look like a ripped viking.

Some things I've learned along my journey:

  • Fuck everyone else. I did this for me. Once I let go of what others thought, it was just me.
  • I don't like gym rats. I do like the overweight people that are trying to make a difference. If the situation allows, I'll call out in passing, "We're in the right place!" "Good job! You're here! You're doing it!" Stuff like that. Stuff I wish people would have said to me.
  • Now that I've lost this weight (and went from a size 46+ waist to a size 33), I have zero tolerance for fat people. It is a choice. If I can do it, so can anyone else. If someone is doing the work, I'll applaud them every step of the way. If someone sits on their fat ass and bitches about "fat is beautiful", then fuck them. Their body will force them to lose weight by having a limb removed through diabetes, all their weight removed when they die from heart disease, etc.
  • I adjusted my program as I felt. I listen to my body. Some days I go heavier on the weights. Other days, I ease up a little bit. Sometimes I do the minimum 6 minute cardio warm-up. Other times, I'll go for miles.

I still have a lot to learn, but god damn, I feel good. I can look at my body in the mirror and not cringe. I feel sexy, feel strong and have energy like I've never had before.

I go walk a couple miles on the treadmill before work a few times a week. I need to lose over 100 pounds and it feels like something I will never accomplish, so I get sad and stop trying. Here's to hoping this is the time I don't give up!
Remember that 90% of weight lose happens in the kitchen. You can do it!
